---
title: "Week 12: The Hidden Epidemic"
---

## Theme: Intimate Partner Violence: Surveillance, Narratives, and Legal
Evidence

Intimate partner violence is systematically underreported in structured
data. Emergency department codes, police records, and death certificates
each capture only a fraction of the true burden. This week we return to
NLP --- applied to IPV case narratives --- to extract injury mechanisms
invisible in ICD codes and examine how narrative-based data is used in
legal proceedings.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Burden of proof in civil IPV litigation; how pattern
evidence from narrative-based data extraction can establish systematic
harm; Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) data collection and reporting
requirements; mandatory reporting laws for IPV in healthcare settings
and their limitations.

**Health Focus:** The surveillance gap between structured ICD-coded IPV
data and actual IPV burden; sex-based differences in injury mechanism
patterns (blunt object trauma, strangulation, weapon use); IPV as a
driver of preterm birth, mental health disorders, and substance use ---
connecting to Week 8 maternal health findings.

**Data:** De-identified IPV ED narrative dataset (Carmen, IRB-approved
subset from NEISS with IPV-coded incidents); NISVS 2023/2024 Data Brief
(cdc.gov/nisvs); HOLC shapefiles for Columbus; CDC SVI 2020.

**R Code:** stringr::str_detect() with regex patterns for IPV mechanism
extraction; tidytext::unnest_tokens() for tokenization;
dplyr::case_when() to classify Object / Action / Location;
sf::st_as_sf() to map geocoded incidents; ggplot2 geom_sf() choropleth;
chisq.test() to test whether mechanism severity differs by HOLC grade.

- Load de-identified IPV ED narrative dataset (Carmen, IRB-approved
  subset)

- Develop and apply keyword-and-regex coding schema for Object / Action
  / Location injury mechanisms

- Aggregate mechanism frequencies by census tract; map using sf +
  ggplot2 choropleth overlaid on SVI

- Overlay IPV cluster map with HOLC grade boundaries; run chi-square
  test for association between mechanism severity and HOLC grade
